html:
The Union of South Africa was a self-governing British dominion from 1910 to 1961, the forerunner of today's republic of South Africa.

It joined four colonies: the Cape, Natal, the Transvaal and the Orange River Colony. The last two had been Boer republics until Britain beat them in the Second Boer War of 1899 to 1902. Union was a deal between British and Afrikaner whites; most Black South Africans had no vote.

  • 1913: the Natives Land Act kept most land for whites.
  • 1915: it took German South West Africa, now Namibia, and later ran it under a League of Nations mandate.
  • 1926 and 1931: full independence in law from Britain.
  • 1948: the National Party won and began apartheid.
  • 1961: it became a republic and left the Commonwealth.

Jan Smuts, twice prime minister, helped found both the League of Nations and the United Nations.
sum: The Union of South Africa was a self-governing British dominion from 1910 to 1961, the forerunner of today's republic of South Africa.
